corrected_draft.title: White House Officials Use Signal for Official Discussion
corrected_draft.description_short: In March 2025, senior Trump administration officials used Signal to discuss military operations in Yemen in a group chat that included a journalist.
corrected_draft.description_medium: In March 2025, senior Trump administration officials used Signal in a group chat to discuss planned military operations in Yemen. The chat accidentally included a journalist, who later reported on the messages. This event is the opposite of the entry’s asserted government-wide ban on encrypted messaging apps. The reviewed evidence supports the use of Signal in this specific discussion, not a ban applying to all federal employees or applications such as WhatsApp.
corrected_draft.description_long: In March 2025, senior Trump administration officials used Signal to discuss planned U.S. military operations in Yemen in a group chat that accidentally included a journalist. Reuters reported that the thread described an imminent bombing campaign against Houthi militants in Yemen. Jeffrey Goldberg of The Atlantic was added to the private chat alongside Vice President JD Vance, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and CIA Director John Ratcliffe. The messages were disclosed publicly by Goldberg on March 24. On March 31, White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt said the White House considered the case closed and that steps had been taken to prevent recurrence. Reuters also reported that House Intelligence Committee Democrats asked for an independent inquiry and that leaders of the Senate Armed Services Committee asked the Pentagon to investigate the leak. The reporting concerns this specific Signal thread; it does not establish a government-wide ban on encrypted messaging.
